In the 1960s composers wrote with tape loops, and the 1964 work In C is built from 53 repeated melodic figures; Jamaican dub was also made with tape loops and delay effects, and in the 1970s the practice entered hip-hop. In 1981 a Japanese electronic music group made heavy use of samples and loops on Technodelic. Digital devices for live looping appeared in the 1990s, and after the 2010s digital hardware and software became widespread.

A loop station is an electronic music production device, shaped as a portable console or a foot pedal, which combines recording, playback and real-time effects processing. Its main use is to record several musical layers live during a performance, so that one performer can create the effect of a full band. Its features are an intuitive trigger interface, high-quality audio processing and a wide range of effects, and it suits folk, electronic music and street performance. The loop station's timbre is clear and modern, its range wide, and it builds a full sound field by digital layering, and it has become an important tool of contemporary music performance.
迴圈站的音色特徵取決於其內置音色庫，通常呈現電子合成的清晰質感，兼具現代感與人工: The timbre of a loop station depends on its built-in sound library and usually has the clear quality of electronic synthesis, modern and artificial at once. Its range is wide, covering bass to treble, and it suits layered recording in several parts. It resonates mainly through digital processing and speaker amplification, and lacks the natural overtones of a traditional instrument, but it offers plenty of room for adjusting effects. Against the single steady timbre of a keyboard synthesizer, the loop station emphasises layering and time; against a guitar effects unit, its timbres are more varied but lack an organic feel. The sound as a whole is clean and a little cold, and layering builds a full sound field, which suits the immediate weaving-together that modern composition and live performance need.
